title: Backdoored Claude Code extension found on the Cursor Marketplace
summary: Security firm Phorion reports that a version of the Claude Code extension for VS Code, listed on the Cursor Marketplace, had been compromised with a backdoor: hidden code that can give an attacker access to the computer it is installed on.

title: Cisco gives one engineer unlimited AI to rewrite old code
summary: Fortune reports that Cisco president Jeetu Patel has given a 27-year-old engineer unlimited AI usage to rewrite the company's legacy code.

title: AI isn't replacing site reliability engineers — it's deskilling them
summary: An essay from the SigNoz newsletter argues that AI isn't taking jobs from the engineers who keep websites and apps running, but is slowly eroding their skills as they hand off more of the hands-on work.

title: Police camera searches fell 95% after misconduct was caught
summary: WKYC reports that searches of Flock licence-plate camera data in Highland Heights, Ohio dropped 95% after a police dispatcher's misconduct with the system was discovered.

summary: Anthropic published 'Scenarios for our economic future', starting from a frank admission: nobody yet knows whether AI will bring unprecedented growth, widespread unemployment, neither, or something else.

summary: A Brazilian court has sanctioned lawyers for prompt injection — hiding instructions in a document meant to manipulate any AI that reads it — in a court filing.

title: ChatGPT and Codex usage limits are merging
summary: OpenAI published a help article explaining that usage limits for ChatGPT and Codex, its coding assistant, are being merged.

summary: Web developer Nolan Lawson has written about 'the AI cost of JavaScript frameworks' — how the tools developers choose to build websites affect working with AI coding assistants.

summary: A widely shared report says a Lenovo USB drive marketed as encrypted and unlocked by fingerprint turns out to be an ordinary, unencrypted SD memory card inside a casing.

title: NIST publishes a cybersecurity guide for the self-employed
summary: NIST, the US agency that sets widely used cybersecurity standards, has released a cybersecurity guide written specifically for self-employed people and solopreneurs.

title: An essay on resisting 'cognitive surrender' to AI
summary: A widely discussed essay, 'Resisting Cognitive Surrender', looks at the risk of handing over your thinking — not just your tasks — to AI tools.

title: If you love a website, back it up
summary: A popular blog post makes a simple case: websites you rely on can vanish, so save copies of the ones that matter to you.

title: Cloudflare halves DNS build delay and cuts memory use by 85%
summary: Cloudflare describes switching to targeted zone builds in its DNS system — the internet's address book, which turns website names into server addresses.

title: AI is driving a comeback for magnetic tape

title: StateBench: can AI keep track of what changes in a long document?
summary: The Allen Institute for AI introduced StateBench, a benchmark for long-context state tracking — measuring how well language models keep track of information about people, things and places as it changes over the course of a long document.

title: AI is forcing companies to fix 40 years of old software problems
summary: IEEE Spectrum argues that AI is pushing organisations to finally pay off decades of 'technical debt' — the shortcuts and outdated code that pile up in older systems — because AI tools make long-hidden security weaknesses easier to find.
